content.title: About
content.content: Green beans (edible pods of the common bean) are young fruits harvested at 8‑12 days of age. Raw beans have a crisp texture, a mildly sweet flavor, and a bright green color. They can be eaten fresh, added to salads and snacks, or briefly cooked for a softer bite.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green beans belong to the legume family and are closely related to peas, lentils, and soy.
Unlike mature beans, green beans are edible raw, though they are often blanched to preserve color and tenderness.
They contain more vitamin C than most other vegetables.
Traditional Asian cuisines use them in stir‑fries and salads with soy‑based dressings.
Green beans can be grown in pots, making them a popular urban‑garden vegetable.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C is a powerful antioxidant that supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Protein in green beans helps maintain muscle mass and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, helps regulate blood sugar, and supports gut health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Green beans are virtually fat‑free, making them suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: High in folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Food poisoning risk
items.content: Raw beans may contain small amounts of phytohemagglutinin, which can be toxic in large quantities. If the beans taste bitter or smell off, it is safer to blanch them.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to legumes and may experience skin rashes or more severe symptoms.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large servings of raw beans can cause gas and bloating due to oligosaccharides.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw green beans can be tossed into salads, blended into smoothies, dipped in hummus, or simply enjoyed as a crunchy snack. For a softer bite, blanch them for 2‑3 minutes and shock in ice water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store green beans in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. They stay fresh for 5‑7 days. Discard any wilted or damaged pods before use.
